 Order

The challenge in the writ petition is to the show cause notice issued by the second respondent based upon the report on the factual premise that the product sold by the petitioner did not meet the standards of a food product.
2. The learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that what the petitioner had sold was Gingelly Lighting Oil and the same cannot be used for consumption.
The label of the bottle had also indicated that the same was not recommended for cooking purposes and is for external use.

When that be so, the entire proceeding initiated against the petitioner is wholly without jurisdiction, as the product of the petitioner at any stretch of imagination will not fall under the definition of food as defined under Section 2(j) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (herein after referred to as FSSAI Act, 2006).
Hence, he would seek to quash the impugned order.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 3.

The learned Additional Government Pleader appearing for the first respondent would submit that the lighting oil was minutely written, which would mislead the consumers to treat it as a Gingelly Oil and to use for cooking purposes.
He would further submit that the label had also contained that the product contained sesame oil, Palmolein Oil and Refined Rice Bran Oil.
When that be so, there has been a misbranding of the product.
Hence, the same would fall within the mischief of Section 23 of FSSAI Act, 2006 and Regulations framed therein relating to packaging and labeling.
Therefore, he would seek this Court to dismiss this writ petition.
4. I have considered the rival submissions made by the learned counsel on either side.
5. The petitioner had only sold the Gingelly oil for lighting purposes.

It is also admitted by the respondents in their counter that the term 'lighting oil' has been inscribed in the label, but was printed in such a small letter, which may lead for consumers buying the same for cooking purposes.
Had the petitioner sold its https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis oil without indicating the same as lighting oil, then one could understand that there has been a misbranding.

Further, the FSSAI Act,
2006 and the Regulations framed thereunder for branding and labelling can only be made applicable to the food product falling within the definition of Section 2(j) of the FSSAI Act, 2006.
In the present case, the product of the petitioner is not a food product, as the same indicates that the product is only for external use and not for cooking purposes.

6. In such view of the matter, the respondents do not have the jurisdiction to initiate any proceedings under the FSSAI Act, 2006 and for that reason, the impugned notice is liable to be set aside and is accordingly set aside.
In fine, the Writ Petition stands allowed.
However, there shall be no order as to costs.
Consequently, connected Miscellaneous Petitions are closed.
